thread:
anya: Quick sync — we need to lock sprint slices for Optimize toolkit. Customer asks (ACMEHealth + two pilots) landed a week ago. Main asks: 1) actionable batching recommendations per workload, 2) prefix/KV cache visibility + auto-suggestion, 3) quantization guidance with perf/quality tradeoffs, 4) eval-triggered alerts for regressions. Thoughts on MVP scope?
liam: +1 to focusing on batching + eval alerts first. Caching UX is tricky but we can ship a minimal telemetry surface.
maya: For quant guidance we need a simple matrix: model family x sequence length -> suggested quant level + expected p95 latency delta + test prompts to validate quality. Can build from existing bench harness.
sofia: From CS: customers want clear guardrails. They asked for an "explainable" rec — why we picked a batch size/quant setting for them. A short rationale string would help.
anya: Good note @sofia. Proposal: split into three deliverables this sprint: A) Batching advisor (heuristic + telemetry) B) Cache visibility (KV hit metrics + one-click enable suggestion) C) Eval-alert plumbing (hook evals -> alerts + alert severity buckets). Quant guidance becomes scope for next sprint unless we shrink B and C.
liam: Implementation risk notes: batching advisor needs runtime hooks for sequence histogram and latency/cost sim. Cache visibility mostly telemetry + UI. Eval-alerts require tying eval outputs to alert rules and slack/email webhooks.
maya: For A we can initially surface a recommend payload like: `{"batch_size": 8, "reason": "median seq 64, p99 latency target 250ms"}` and a small CLI to run local sim.
alex: UX: keep UI card compact. Suggested micro-copy: "We recommend batch_size=8 — expected cost -21%, median latency +40ms vs per-request. Why: typical 60-80 token calls in last 24h."
sofia: Can we expose a rollback toggle? Customers want an easy way to revert advices.
liam: Yes — config will be a recommendation only unless user flips "auto-apply". We'll include an explicit revert flag.
anya: Who owns the acceptance criteria? Draft below — please call out missing items.
anya: ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (draft):
- Batching advisor: shows recommended batch_size and expected cost/latency delta, backed by 24h histogram; recommendation toggled on/off; CLI sim reproduces numbers.
- Cache visibility: KV hit/miss rate in console + top-5 prefixes by volume + a single action "Suggest cache hint" that generates a one-line suggestion.
- Eval-alerts: can create an alert triggered by an eval suite failing threshold; severity routing to #optimize-alerts and to ops-email; alert contains failing prompt examples.
- Docs: Quickstart + one-pager describing heuristics.
- Tests: e2e for each flow + unit tests for thresholding logic.
liam: Missing SLO/backfill: Do we need a default threshold set? I can add sane defaults: 10% drop in f1 or 5% increase in hallucination score -> warn, 20% drop -> critical.
maya: Agree. Also metric definitions must be explicit in docs.
sofia: From pilot customers: they will only opt-in if the first week shows <5% false positives on alerts. Can we include a short trial window where alerts are 'informational' for 7 days?
anya: Yes — add "dry-run" mode for alerts for 7 days post-enable.
liam: Timeline ask: we can aim to ship A+B limited beta by EOW sprint (two-week sprint) if we carve quant out. Eval-alerts basic plumbing likely lands mid-sprint.
anya: Okay. Action items: @liam own A+B infra + API, @maya own eval metric defs + quant roadmap doc, @alex own UI card + copy, @sofia run pilot comms and acceptance. I'll draft PRD after this thread and drop link.
deploy-bot: new-deploy queued for branch optimize/batching-advisor (ci: green) :rocket:
sofia: I'll reach back to ACMEHealth and Pilot2 to confirm dry-run acceptance and share acceptance checklist.
anya: Great — let's reconvene Thurs 1pm to sign off. If anyone sees major blockers before then @anya. :thumbsup:
